sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

stage_1.expense_line_item: NUANS corporate name search and preliminary reservation (one-hour window, Alberta Corporate Registry)
stage_1.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Authorized Service Provider (Creyos? e.g., Ownr)
stage_1.legal_fee_basis: Statutory government fee (CAD ~40) as set out in the Corporate Registry Regulation; service provider surcharge at market

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 1, 12, 15, 17, 101, 104, 110 and the Business Corporations Regulation, Alta Reg 119/2021
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 3) under the Alberta Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; no escrow account or capital deposit is required for incorporation. SPAC offering proceeds, if any, must be segregated in a Canadian banking trust or escrow arrangement under applicable securities regulatory requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD MEETING OF [INSERT CORPORATE NAME], a corporation incorporated under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. After due notice to all directors, the board unanimously resolves: (1) Share Subscription: the corporation accepts the share subscription of the founding shareholder and directors; the subscribed common shares are allotted and issued as fully paid. (2) Registered Office: the registered office at [INSERT ADDRESS IN ALBERTA] is adopted and filed with the Registrar for service. (3) Officers: the President, Secretary, and Treasurer are appointed to maintain corporate records and to execute banking, securities, and escrow arrangements. All actions are effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Pre-Clearance and NUANS Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via Corporate Access online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed corporate name; verify that the proposed name is not confusingly similar to any existing registered name; if the name incorporates any regulated word or phrase, file supporting consents; reserve the approved name, if desired, by filing the statutory name reservation form and paying the applicable fee.
required_dossiers: Consent to Use of Corporate Name (if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a revised name reservation with a new NUANS report; no automatic review exists, so a fresh application and applicable fee must be submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Articles of Incorporation (Form 3) reflecting corporate name, registered office address, share structure and class restrictions, director count, and permitted business restrictions; where required, attach signed director consents and a Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors; file online through Corporate Registry; upon approval, issuance of a Certificate of Incorporation creates the corporation’s legal existence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Corporate Registry issues a correction or rejection notice, cure the defect by filing amended articles or supplying supplementary information within the prescribed response period; re-file upon failure of electronic validation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Share Subscription and Escrow Account Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Canadian chartered bank or trust company acting as escrow agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Record the take-up of issued common shares by founders or initial subscribers in the share register; pass a board resolution authorizing the escrow account and deposit of public offering proceeds, if any, in accordance with the SPAC prospectus and Alberta securities requirements; ensure subscriptions are paid into a segregated trust account designated for funds pending completion of a qualifying acquisition.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the financial institution queries the escrow mandate, deliver a certified copy of the board resolution and the executed escrow agreement; a revised resolution may be signed if the account structure must be amended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene First Board Meeting and Adopt Organizational Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent of directors; adopt the pro-forma first board resolution confirming share subscription, registered office, appointment of officers, approval of the corporate seal, and selection of the fiscal year-end; also authorize execution of banking, securities regulatory, and escrow documentation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a board quorum is challenged, reconvene with proper notice or obtain a new unanimous written consent from all incumbent directors; any resolution defect is cured by a subsequent ratification resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the federal CRA business number through CRA Business Registration Online after receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation; register the corporate income tax account, and, if applicable, GST/HST, payroll, and Alberta corporate tax accounts; provide the registered office address and officer information required for tax correspondence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA returns an incomplete record, contact the Business Registration Service team, resubmit the missing attestation, and align the entity details with the Certificate of Incorporation; corrections are accepted without penalty where made within the CRA response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Securities Reporting Issuer Clearance and SPAC Licensing Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the SPAC preliminary prospectus and any prescribed disclosure documents with the ASC; respond to ASC comments until a final receipt is obtained, thereby qualifying the issuer as a reporting issuer; if the corporation intends to list, apply to the applicable exchange and coordinate the final prospectus and escrowed funds release conditions.
required_dossiers: Audited Financial Statements or Auditors’ Comfort Letter
Escrow Agreement and Escrow Agent Acknowledgment
Directors’ and Officers’ Personal Information Forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ASC issues a comment letter, submit amended disclosure and legal responses; the waiting period may be recommenced until comments are cleared, and any materially misleading filing must be withdrawn and refiled with corrected information.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Securities Commission (ASC) for statutory securities authorization, with no physical industrial licensing board applicable to an office-only SPAC vehicle
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Reporting Issuer Status by Final Prospectus Receipt under the Securities Act (Alberta), and exchange listing approval if publicly traded

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical works, designated industrial activity, or project development; administrative office activity only
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; no wastewater, VOC, or industrial waste thresholds triggered. Electronic waste and office consumables, if generated, are managed under Alberta’s Recycling Regulation and municipal waste bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial fire safety, structural load, or civil defense certification is required for an office-only SPAC. The premises must comply with Alberta Fire Code occupancy standards; employers must maintain Workers’ Compensation Board coverage, Occupational Health and Safety incident reporting, and general workplace clearance obligations under the OHS Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and My Business Account (MyBA); https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident SPAC incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Alberta Business Corporations Act must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA. File Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) electronically via BRO or by mail/courier to the CRA's Business Accounts Registration desk, providing the Articles of Incorporation, Alberta Extra-Provincial Registration Certificate (if federally incorporated), registered office address in Alberta, and the name and address of the authorized Canadian representative for service. The CRA issues the 15-character BN (9-digit base plus the 2-letter program account suffix) upon approval; the RC1 program account is the corporate income tax account (administered by CRA for both federal and Alberta provincial corporate income tax under the collection agreement), and the RT program account is the GST/HST account. Registration is required within 30 days of making the first taxable supply in Canada; GST/HST registration is mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 over any period of four consecutive calendar quarters or a single calendar quarter. A SPAC may also voluntarily register for GST/HST to claim input tax credits on IPO and due-diligence costs, subject to the exempt financial services restrictions. The same BN serves as the statutory TIN for corporate income tax and as the VAT ID for GST/HST purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not offer a US-style check-the-box election; every corporation is a statutory taxpayer under the Income Tax Act and the Excise Tax Act. Elections relevant to a foreign-owned SPAC include: (i) the subsection 211(1) GST/HST election for closely related corporations to treat certain intercompany supplies as made for nil consideration, which is valuable when an acquisition target trust or escrow structure is used; (ii) a substitutional tax year end election under section 142.2(1)(a) where applicable, subject to CRA acceptance; (iii) a Part XIII treaty-based withholding relief election via Form NR301 for payments to the foreign parent; and (iv) a designation of the SPAC's representative under section 142.1 of the Excise Tax Act for non-resident registrants. Hybrid mismatch rules (sections 18.2, 18.3, 20.2 of the Income Tax Act) and the Excessive Interest and Financing Expenses Limitation (EIFEL) rules (sections 18.21-18.23) are mandatory and do not permit an elective opt-out. The small business deduction rate reduction is unavailable to a SPAC because it does not carry on an active business.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Alberta is a non-participating province, so only the 5% federal GST applies and no provincial sales tax is levied.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small supplier threshold, computed on the SPAC's worldwide taxable supplies together with associated entities, over the four preceding calendar quarters). A non-resident SPAC making taxable supplies in Canada must register for GST/HST irrespective of the threshold if it is engaged in an adventure or concern in the nature of trade involving Canadian real property or makes a prescribed supply of real property in Canada; a SPAC holding an escrow/trust in Canada may have Canadian reporting obligations even without regular supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API invoice-approval regime. Mandatory electronic filing applies to GST/HST registrants whose total annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1,000,000 (returns filed via CRA Netfile), and to all T2 corporate income tax filers with gross revenue over CAD 1,000,000. Standard GST/HST invoice content requirements (BN of the supplier, date, description, and tax amount) are enforceable, but there is no pre-clearance portal. Registrants must retain auditable electronic records, including the underlying export documentation, EDI messages, and bank wire proofs, for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada are zero-rated under section 16 and Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act, and services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated where the service is performed wholly or substantially outside Canada (Schedule VI, Part V, section 7) or where the supply is of an intangible to a non-resident and not for use in Canada. For a SPAC, custodial, trust, underwriting, and share-issuance services are financial services under Schedule VI, Part VII and are EXEMPT, not zero-rated; accordingly the SPAC generally cannot claim 0% GST on its service fee streams and its input tax credit eligibility is restricted under the exempt-supply de minimis rules. To claim zero-rating on any qualifying corporate export transaction, the SPAC must be a GST/HST registrant, hold contemporaneous evidence of physical export or offshore performance, and demonstrate that the supply was made to a resident of a foreign country in the ordinary course of its commercial activities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency ACI/eManifest export report with unique transaction reference)
Bill of Lading (negotiable or straight, showing the SPAC as shipper and the foreign recipient as consignee)
Commercial Invoice with Incoterms, description, quantity, and foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 bank statement evidencing foreign currency proceeds credited to the SPAC's Canadian bank account
Export Evidence Worksheet (CRA GST/HST Memorandum 17.4 exhibit) signed by the SPAC officer
Freight Forwarder's Certificate of Export or carrier airway bill confirmation when a third-party logistics provider is used
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA large-business audit programs focus on SPAC structures because net tax refunds and ITC claims on pre-IPO and acquisition costs are frequently traced. Where zero-rating is claimed without the statutory export bundle, CRA will reassess the supply at 5% GST, deny the associated ITC refund, and apply interest compounded daily at the prescribed rate. A gross-negligence penalty of 25% of the falsely claimed refund (minimum CAD 250) applies under section 285.1 of the Excise Tax Act; the late-filing/reporting penalty under section 280 adds 1% of the net tax plus 0.25% per month up to 12 months. Fraudulent evasion is prosecuted under section 327, with summary conviction fines up to CAD 200,000 and/or five years' imprisonment and, on indictment, fines up to CAD 1,000,000 and/or five years. The normal four-year reassessment window is extended indefinitely in cases of misrepresentation made fraudulently or with gross negligence. For a SPAC, clawback risk is heightened where trust, escrow, and broker fees are characterized as exempt financial services rather than zero-rated exports, rendering any 0% claim ineligible ab initio.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under the International Monetary Fund Article VIII status. The Canadian dollar floats freely; there are no general restrictions on the conversion of CAD to foreign currency for trade or investment. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is legally permitted via dividends, interest, royalties, or management fees, subject to Canadian federal withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act and applicable double taxation treaty relief. For a SPAC vehicle, repatriation of escrowed IPO proceeds and M&A target funding are treated as capital transactions and are not subject to exchange control licensing, though Canada's anti-money laundering and sanctions reporting obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and the Criminal Code apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation, or conversion requirements for export proceeds. There is no statutory timeline requiring exporters to bring foreign currency receipts into Canada, and entities are free to maintain foreign currency accounts domestically or abroad. Reporting obligations arise only under the Income Tax Act for foreign-source income, the FATCA/CRS framework for financial accounts, and the Currency and Foreign Transactions Reporting Act counterpart rules for cross-border transfers exceeding CAD 10,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs). Canada does not recognize the EMI licence; an entity seeking to offer payment accounts or issue e-money must be a bank under the Bank Act, a credit union, or a registered payment service provider under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) once fully in force. Offshore EMIs generally cannot obtain a Canadian banking licence without substantial physical presence and prudential regulation by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). An unregulated offshore EMI may apply for registration as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC, but such registration does not confer deposit-taking authority. For a SPAC treasury, relying on offshore EMIs for escrow or capital preservation is not viable; they may be used only for auxiliary cross-border payment aggregation subject to FINTRAC MSB compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the PCMLTFA and OSFI guidance, banks are required to identify and verify all directors, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners using reliable, independent source documents. In practice, Tier-1 Canadian banks require at least one director with signing authority to attend an in-person onboarding interview at a Canadian branch or via an approved Canadian notary representative. Fully remote opening is rare for a non-resident SPAC unless the entity has pre-existing Canadian banking relationships and all directors hold valid Canadian government-issued ID. Where foreign directors are present, the bank typically requires a physical interview at the local branch plus certified passport copies, corporate resolution, and foreign legal opinion. The presence of a registered agent in Alberta is insufficient to waive the in-person requirement for the ultimate controller; it is prudent to plan for an in-country KYC interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: SPAC or blank-check company in the public listing pipeline, which is associated with higher securities fraud and money laundering typologies due to unvetted investors, undisclosed SPAC sponsors, and unstable use of escrowed proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the executed final prospectus or offering memorandum, notice of public offering, securities commission filing confirmation (SEC Form 20-F, Form F-1, or Canadian equivalent); escrow agreement with a licensed Canadian trust company; detailed use-of-proceeds schedule; sponsor/management agreement; and FINTRAC customer risk rating rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or multi-tiered corporate chain where ultimate owners are in non-Egmont or tax-haven jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit an updated organizational chart identifying every shareholder with a 25% or greater ownership interest; certified share register; government-issued photo ID and proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner; Alberta Corporate Registry / Corporations Canada attestation; and a written declaration of no nominee shareholding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow account structure with a third-party trustee or custodian holding capital injection and public offering proceeds outside the direct control of the banked entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full trust deed, escrow/custody agreement, verification of the trustee's regulatory licence, trustee undertaking to withhold funds until closing conditions, independent audit confirmation of segregated balances, and legal counsel opinion confirming that the escrow structure does not contravene Canadian securities or trust-law requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border inbound wire transfers from Cayman Islands, BVI, or other high-risk jurisdictions for IPO subscription or M&A bridge financing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver source-of-funds documentation including the subscription agreement, investor questionnaire, placement agency agreement, and U.S. or Cayman regulatory status; original wire instructions containing full legal name and LEI of the remitter; bank statements evidencing the origin of the funds; and FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction Report and international funds transfer reports when thresholds are met.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and absence of substantive physical operational presence in Alberta creating concern over intended jurisdiction of banking activities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce a registered office lease in Alberta with productive use; minutes of board meetings held in Canada; audited or review-engagement financial statements prepared by a Canadian CPA; annual beneficial ownership return filed with Alberta corporate registry; directors' passports and work permit/residency cards; and a detailed business continuity plan showing the SPAC's Canadian nexus.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital routing for SPAC injections should use SWIFT MT103/MT202 with the full legal name and Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) of the sending and receiving entities. The Canadian receiving bank must be notified in advance with the account number, bank branch, and purpose code. In Canada, inbound cross-border wire payments are classified under Statistics Canada's Cross-Border Wire Reporting framework; the purpose code for securities transactions or capital investments should be used where applicable (e.g., 'Securities Purchase' or 'Investment in Issuer'). The sending financial institution should include a clear narrative in the wire such as 'SPAC IPO escrow contribution' or 'Share subscription proceeds', and the receiving bank will verify against sanctions lists (OSFI/DFATD), FATCA/CRS, and the Bank of Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) rules. Where the amount exceeds CAD 10,000, the receiving bank must file an International Electronic Funds Transfer Report with FINTRAC and may request the underlying subscription agreement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for target acquisitions should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for low-value or non-LC transactions, and MT202 COV for interbank cover payments. For large-value CAD payments, use the Lynx payment system (formerly LVTS) to settle in central-bank money. For cross-border USD, the Canadian bank will typically clear through CHIPS (Clearing House Interbank Payments System) or correspondent banking via SWIFT. Commercial letters of credit (LC) are permissible for trade-related disbursements, particularly when acquiring cross-border operating assets; standby LCs may back the performance obligations of the SPAC. All outbound wires must include an accurate transaction purpose code, CRS/FATCA indicators, and a reference to the underlying acquisition agreement to satisfy the receiving bank's KYC screening and Canadian AML obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD spot and outright forward contracts
Cross-currency swaps for merger closing and capital account hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for illiquid emerging market target jurisdictions where CAD/USD/conversion is restricted

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific tax incentives for SPACs; general deductions available. Alberta small business rate of 2% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income may apply if eligible, but SPACs typically not eligible.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed via CRA's My Business Account or approved e-file software (NETFILE for corporations)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian-source revenue only; attach T106 if cross-border transactions exceed thresholds.
Ensure expenses are reasonable and supported; disallow non-arm's length payments without proper documentation.
Apply treaty provisions if applicable; claim foreign tax credits for taxes paid to other jurisdictions.
Calculate using applicable rates; consider provincial allocation rules for Alberta.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of balance owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months. Additional penalties for failure to file information returns (e.g., T106) up to CAD 2,500 per return.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form NR301 (Application for Treaty-Based Waiver) or provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) to the withholding agent; for US residents, use Form W-8BEN-E. Treaty rates vary by jurisdiction; e.g., US dividends 15% (5% for substantial shareholding).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% domestic, reduced to 10% under US treaty (0% for certain IP). Interest: 25% domestic, reduced to 0% under US treaty (subject to conditions).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million for goods, CAD 500,000 for services/interest/royalties (threshold for filing T106); Master File and Local File required if total revenue exceeds CAD 5 million and cross-border transactions exceed CAD 5 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and treaty abuse provisions apply. SPACs must demonstrate commercial substance to avoid being deemed a conduit or sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful evasion of tax by underreporting income, claiming false deductions, or failing to file returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 200% of tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years, and interest on unpaid amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes under Section 227.1 of the Income Tax Act if they failed to withhold or remit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a SPAC without economic substance, engaging in artificial transactions to avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment, penalties under GAAR, and potential denial of treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly participated in the scheme; civil restitution may be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), including inadequate KYC or reporting of suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CAD 2 million per violation for corporations, imprisonment for individuals, and suspension of operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for AML penalties if they consented or were negligent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's length pricing on cross-border transactions not at arm's length rates, without proper documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties up to 10% of net adjustment, and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they participated in the pricing decision; travel bans may be imposed for egregious cases.
